hypothesis: The unchanged bidirectional breakout-onset provider can be evaluated as a shared-account live-research mechanism on BTC, ETH, SOL, and HYPE while prospectively testing whether side-aligned visible-book pressure identifies after-cost opportunities currently withheld only because the completed 5-minute state is not BREAKOUT.
decision: Keep the authorized v14 runtime, open protected SOL lifecycle, exact 5-minute breakout gate, cooldown, sizing, and exits unchanged. Freeze two report-only aligned-book challengers at 2026-08-06T22:08:00Z: one on HYPE and one on SOL, each bidirectional, $75 hypothetical notional, 60-minute horizon, 80-bps adverse-BBO stop proxy, full taker fees, official funding, and flat-symbol portfolio compatibility. Earlier same-run discovery was favorable only for shorts and sparse—HYPE 4W/1L across five aligned paths and SOL 2W/1L across three—so it is hypothesis-formation evidence rather than forward proof. Exclude every pre-cutoff path, keep candidate outcomes non-additive to live PnL, and grant no execution authority.
falsifier: Reject or materially weaken either challenger if its fresh deployable after-cost profit factor is at or below one, total net return is nonpositive, one path dominates absolute outcomes, top-level capacity or realistic costs consume the edge, or both directions are not eventually represented without a pre-registered structural explanation. The experiment contract is invalidated by accepting pre-cutoff candidates, counting a SOL candidate while SOL is already occupied as deployable, pooling overlapping HYPE and SOL outcomes as portfolio PnL, changing the blocker or OPI threshold after outcomes, or granting order, sizing, exit, promotion, or execution authority.
limitations: Discovery contains only five HYPE and three SOL resolved aligned-book paths, all short, from one partial live day; it cannot establish a bidirectional repeatable edge.
The discovery matrix uses recorded BBO replay and official funding rather than private IOC fills; top-level capacity is enforced but latency and adverse selection remain estimates.
The prospective observers use a fixed 60-minute horizon and 80-bps adverse-BBO stop proxy; they test entry selection rather than the deployed 8-to-24-hour exit controller.
The first post-cutoff HYPE candidate is pending, while the first SOL candidate conflicts with the real open SOL position and is therefore not deployable portfolio evidence.
The mutable runtime observer outputs are deliberately excluded from immutable evidence references; later outcome revisions must bind immutable prefix snapshots.
One evidence file cited by historical revision 1 later changed and remains visibly reported as integrity drift; revision 8 does not conceal or reinterpret that prior defect.
No strategy, position, order, sizing policy, execution scope, venue stop, backend process, or current portfolio configuration changed as a result of this revision.
